description:
A fortress at Rosenau is recorded in 1194, when Hadmar II of Kuenring handed it to the bishopric of Passau as a fief, according to regional sources. Count Leopold Christoph Schallenberg, a courtier in the time of Maria Theresa, had the building rebuilt in 1736–1747 as the present Baroque castle, to plans by the architect Josef Munggenast.

Schallenberg set up a Masonic lodge in the castle in the 18th century. The State of Lower Austria took over the castle in 1964 and had it restored, and during the works the frescoes of the old lodge room were uncovered. The castle now houses the Austrian Freemasonry Museum, opened in the 1970s.

Today the castle also operates as a four-star castle hotel with a restaurant, a small wellness area and a green park, south-west of the town of Zwettl in the Waldviertel.
history: A fortress at Rosenau is recorded in 1194, and the estate later passed to the Schallenberg family. Count Leopold Christoph Schallenberg had it rebuilt in 1736–1747 as the present Baroque castle, to plans by Josef Munggenast, and set up a Masonic lodge in it. In 1964 the State of Lower Austria took over the castle and restored it; the frescoes of the lodge room came to light during the works, and the Austrian Freemasonry Museum opened there in the 1970s. Today the castle also operates as a hotel.

faqs.question: Why is there a Freemasonry Museum at Schloss Rosenau?
faqs.answer: Count Leopold Christoph Schallenberg set up a Masonic lodge in the castle in the 18th century. Its frescoes were uncovered during the restoration after 1964, and the Austrian Freemasonry Museum opened there in the 1970s.

faqs.question: Who designed Schloss Rosenau?
faqs.answer: The Baroque castle was rebuilt in 1736–1747 to plans by Josef Munggenast for Count Leopold Christoph Schallenberg.

meta_title: Rosenau Castle, Waldviertel — Baroque Castle Hotel and Freemasonry Museum
meta_description: Stay at Rosenau Castle, a Baroque castle in the Waldviertel near Zwettl, Austria — a four-star castle hotel with a Freemasonry Museum. From approx. €258/night.

hotel.non_guest_access_note: The castle houses the Austrian Freemasonry Museum, which can be visited separately; check its opening times before you go.
hotel.room_location_note: Rooms are in the castle and its outbuildings; ask the hotel which building your room is in
hotel.how_to_stay:
**Getting there:** The castle stands in the village of Schloss Rosenau, about 5 km south-west of Zwettl in the Waldviertel of Lower Austria. Booking lists free private parking, including accessible parking.

**Rooms & rates:** From approx. €258/night for a 25 m² Classic Double Room with a queen bed, a lake and garden view, a private bathroom, a flat-screen TV, a minibar and free Wi-Fi, with breakfast and free cancellation included on the rate seen (no prepayment); larger Comfort and Superior Double Rooms were around €270. Booking shows a small tax charge (about €5) separately, plus a possible member discount that is not included here.

**On-site:** A restaurant, a wellness area with a sauna and massages, the castle park, the Austrian Freemasonry Museum, free parking and free Wi-Fi.

**Good to know:** Rates were seen for one December 2026 night, so check your own dates on Booking; Booking showed no availability for late January. The Freemasonry Museum has its own opening times, so check them before you go.

**Combine with:** [More castle hotels in Austria](/castle-hotels/austria).
